text:
maria: quick FYI — discovered a dead link on the runbook under /runbooks/kv-cache.md. The anchor ‘KV cache tuning’ goes to a 404 when you follow it from the troubleshooting flow.

josh: thanks for flagging. can you paste the exact path or link so i can open a quick PR?

maria: sure — clicking the second paragraph's link (the one that says `KV cache tuning`) directs to `/docs/runtime/kv-cache-tuning` which returns 404 in staging and prod. here's the snippet i used to find it: 
```bash
curl -I https://docs.redwood.ai/runtime/kv-cache-tuning
# HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
```

kevin: i can take this. looks like the file was moved during the runbook restructure. i’ll search the repo and either add a redirect or fix the anchor. prefer redirect?

olivia: redirect is probably the least risky if there was a rename. but if the content moved, mapping to the new anchor is better long-term.

josh: @kevin go with redirect first so ingesters are stable — then follow up with a small PR to update the runbook link target and add a test. ping me on the PR. :+1:

kb-bot: docs-scan detected: runbook anchor 404 (severity: low) — ticket #DOCS-824 created. Assigned to nobody.

kevin: ack — will open 2 PRs: 1) redirect in static config, 2) runbook anchor update + tiny unit test. PRs later today, ETA 3pm PT. tagging @josh for review.

maria: amazing, thanks! if you want a quick grep command to find stray uses: 
```bash
grep -R "kv-cache-tuning" -n docs/ || true
```

josh: also, can we add an owners line in that runbook header if none exists? makes followups easier.

kevin: good call. i'll add CODEOWNERS entry if the file lives under docs/runtime/* and add a small note in the PR description.

olivia: thanks team. remember to link the DOCS-824 ticket in the PR. that helps triage automation. :sparkles:
